title: SQL Injection
description: The application builds SQL queries by concatenating user-controlled input without parameterisation. An attacker can alter the structure of the query sent to the database.
impact: An unauthenticated attacker can read, modify or delete data in the backend database, bypass authentication, and depending on the database configuration execute operating system commands on the database server.
remediation: Use parameterised queries (prepared statements) or a safe ORM API for every database call. Never build SQL from string concatenation. Apply least privilege to the database account used by the application and validate input against an allow-list where possible.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: User-supplied input is reflected into the HTML response without context-appropriate output encoding, allowing injection of arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the victim's browser.
impact: An attacker who convinces a user to follow a crafted link can execute script in the context of the application: stealing session data not protected by HttpOnly, performing actions as the victim, or presenting fraudulent content.
remediation: Encode all untrusted data for the output context (HTML body, attribute, JavaScript, URL). Prefer frameworks that auto-escape by default. Deploy a restrictive Content-Security-Policy as defence in depth.

title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Input submitted by one user is stored by the application and later rendered to other users without output encoding, so injected script runs in every viewer's browser.
impact: Script executes automatically for every user who views the affected page, including administrators, enabling account takeover and actions performed on behalf of victims at scale.
remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding when rendering stored data, sanitise any user-supplied HTML with a maintained allow-list sanitiser, and deploy a restrictive Content-Security-Policy.

title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR)
description: The application uses client-supplied identifiers to access objects without verifying that the authenticated user is authorised to access that specific object.
impact: An authenticated user can read or modify data belonging to other users or tenants by changing an identifier in the request.
remediation: Enforce object-level authorisation on the server for every request that references an object, deriving ownership from the authenticated session rather than from client input. Add automated tests for cross-user access.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
description: The application fetches a URL supplied by the user from the server side without restricting the destination.
impact: An attacker can make the server send requests to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints, potentially exposing credentials and internal data or pivoting into the internal network.
remediation: Allow-list permitted destinations, resolve and validate the target IP after DNS resolution, block private, loopback and link-local ranges, disable redirects, and require IMDSv2 on cloud instances.

title: Missing HTTP Security Headers
description: Responses do not set one or more recommended security headers such as Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options or frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options.
impact: The absence of these headers removes browser-side defence in depth, increasing the impact of other vulnerabilities such as XSS, clickjacking and protocol downgrade.
remediation: Configure the web server or application framework to emit a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security with an appropriate max-age, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and frame-ancestors 'none' (or 'self').

title: Weak TLS Configuration
description: The service accepts deprecated protocol versions (SSLv3, TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1) and/or weak cipher suites.
impact: A network-positioned attacker may be able to downgrade or weaken the encrypted channel, increasing the risk of traffic interception.
remediation: Disable SSLv3, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1. Support TLS 1.2 with AEAD cipher suites and TLS 1.3. Use a maintained configuration baseline such as the Mozilla server-side TLS guidelines.

title: Default or Weak Credentials
description: An administrative interface or service accepted vendor-default or trivially guessable credentials.
impact: An unauthenticated attacker can take full administrative control of the affected system.
remediation: Change all default credentials before deployment, enforce a strong password policy, restrict management interfaces to administrative networks and enable multi-factor authentication where supported.

title: SMB Signing Not Required
description: Hosts on the internal network do not require SMB message signing.
impact: An attacker on the internal network who can coerce or capture authentication (for example through LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning) can relay NTLM authentication to these hosts and execute code or access files as the relayed user.
remediation: Enable 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)' via Group Policy for all workstations and servers, and prioritise domain controllers and file servers.

title: LLMNR / NBT-NS Poisoning
description: Hosts fall back to Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution and NetBIOS Name Service when DNS fails, and trust any responder on the local segment.
impact: An attacker on the local network can answer these broadcast queries, capture NetNTLMv2 hashes for offline cracking, or relay authentication to other hosts.
remediation: Disable LLMNR via Group Policy ('Turn off multicast name resolution') and disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP on all interfaces (DHCP option or adapter settings).

title: Kerberoastable Service Accounts
description: User accounts with Service Principal Names set have weak passwords, allowing any domain user to request service tickets and crack them offline.
impact: Any authenticated domain user can recover the plaintext password of the affected service accounts, which frequently hold elevated privileges.
remediation: Use Group Managed Service Accounts where possible. Otherwise set long (25+ character) random passwords on SPN-bearing accounts, prefer AES encryption types, remove unnecessary SPNs and monitor for anomalous TGS requests.

title: Outdated Software with Known Vulnerabilities
description: The identified service is running a version that is no longer supported or has publicly disclosed vulnerabilities.
impact: Publicly known vulnerabilities often have working exploits available, lowering the skill required to compromise the system.
remediation: Upgrade to a supported, patched release. Establish a patch management process with defined SLAs and maintain an accurate software inventory.

title: Publicly Accessible Cloud Storage Bucket
description: A cloud object storage bucket allows anonymous listing and/or reading of objects.
impact: Anyone on the internet can enumerate and download the stored data.
remediation: Enable account-level public access blocking, remove public ACLs and bucket policies granting access to anonymous principals, and review bucket contents for exposed sensitive data.

title: Username Enumeration
description: The login, registration or password reset functionality responds differently for valid and invalid usernames.
impact: An attacker can build a list of valid accounts to target with password spraying or phishing.
remediation: Return identical responses, status codes and timing for valid and invalid accounts, and combine with rate limiting and account lockout monitoring.
